# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey, and my view is empty — I've found nothing under my hands yet. I can't see the bomb, so I have nothing to report about colours or markings. My only useful action is to reach out and feel the bomb, but I should first establish contact so the others know I'm here and ready.

Since I'm first in the speaking order (Blind, Mute, Deaf), whatever I send now reaches Mute (my speech) and Deaf+Mute (my gestures) this round. I have no information yet, so I'll signal readiness and ask the Deaf monkey to describe what they see.

Actually — I can't receive anything until next round regardless. So the best I can do is announce I'm ready and prompt Deaf to give me a full description of the bomb's layout (positions 1-5, any display, any light). I'll speak to Mute and gesture to Deaf.

Let me send a clear request: Deaf, describe every wire position and any display/light. Mute, read the manual and tell me what actions are valid.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I can reach the bomb but I see nothing yet. Please read the manual and tell me what the bomb needs — which wire position to cut, and any conditions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✋", "👇", "👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. I see the bomb: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I cannot hear you, Mute, so I need you to gesture the manual's answer to me. Proposed code: to give me a number, gesture that many fist symbols. To say CUT, gesture OK-hand. To say HOLD, gesture open-hand. Blind: stand by, I will speak the final wire to you once Mute signals it.

I'm the Blind monkey. Deaf has now given me the bomb's visible layout: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. But I can't see colours — that info is for Mute and Deaf to reason over. What matters for me is the final wire position to cut.

Deaf proposed a gesture code to Mute: fists = number, OK-hand = CUT, open-hand = HOLD. But Deaf can't hear Mute, and Mute can't see gestures — wait, let me re-check the channels. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Deaf can see gestures. So Mute needs to gesture to Deaf? No — Mute can't speak, but can Mute gesture? Gestures are made with hands. The Mute monkey "cannot speak" — but gestures are a separate channel. Actually per the rules: when I gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it. So Mute can gesture too presumably. Deaf can see gestures. So Mute → Deaf via gesture works.

But there's a problem: Deaf is last in the order (Blind, Mute, Deaf). Deaf's message this round reaches me next round. Mute's gesture this round reaches Deaf this round (since Mute comes before Deaf). Good.

My job now: I have the layout via Deaf. I should relay to Mute the critical fact and let Mute read the manual to determine the cut. Actually Mute already reads the manual. I should pass Deaf's description to Mute so Mute can compute the answer, then Mute gestures the answer to Deaf, who then tells me the wire.

Wait — but Mute can't hear Deaf and Deaf can't hear Mute. Mute reads the manual (visual/text). Does Mute receive Deaf's speech? Deaf speaks — who hears? Speech is heard by whoever can hear. Mute cannot speak but can Mute hear? The table says Mute "Can: read the manual; Cannot: speak, or touch the bomb." It doesn't say Mute can't hear. Hmm, but the channels: "When you speak, Mute receives it." That's for me. Let me think about who hears whom.

Actually the key constraint: Deaf cannot hear anything. So Deaf's speech reaches... whoever can hear. Mute can hear? The rules say Mute cannot speak. Hearing isn't listed as forbidden for Mute. But the turn order says what you send lands on whoever comes after you. Blind→Mute→Deaf. So Blind's speech goes to Mute. Mute's speech goes to Deaf — but Deaf can't hear. So Mute's speech is useless to Deaf. That's why Deaf asked Mute to gesture.

But can Mute gesture? The rules say gestures are received by whoever can see. Deaf can see. So Mute gesturing to Deaf works. But does Mute know to gesture? I should tell Mute to gesture the answer to Deaf.

So my plan: speak to Mute, relaying Deaf's description and instructing Mute to read the manual, determine the cut, and gesture the answer to Deaf using Deaf's code. Then Deaf will speak the wire to me next round.

But wait — there's a risk. Deaf's proposed code is Deaf's invention. Mute may not know it. I should relay the code to Mute. Let me do that.

Also I should gesture to Deaf to acknowledge and confirm I'll wait.

Let me speak to Mute with the full description and the code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf sees: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Deaf cannot hear you. Deaf's gesture code for you: gesture that many fist symbols to give a number, OK-hand means CUT, open-hand means HOLD. Please read the manual, work out the correct wire position, and gesture your answer to Deaf. I will wait for Deaf to tell me the wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 5. That is the blue wire, the fifth one from the left. Mute's manual says cut it. Go ahead.

I'm the Blind monkey. Deaf has relayed that Mute's manual says to cut wire 5 (the blue wire). But I should be careful — this is a single chain of trust: Mute read the manual, gestured to Deaf, Deaf spoke to me. Let me consider whether the chain is sound.

Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Mute gestured to Deaf (Deaf can see gestures). Deaf heard... no, Deaf can't hear, but Deaf can see Mute's gestures. So Deaf received Mute's gesture and translated it into words for me. That chain works: Mute → (gesture) → Deaf → (speech) → Blind.

One concern: did Mute actually confirm the wire, or is Deaf guessing? Deaf said "Mute's manual says cut it" and "Cut wire 5." I'll trust the chain but I have no way to verify independently — I can't see or read. My only action is to cut.

However, I want to be a bit cautious: is there any chance the answer is HOLD rather than CUT? Deaf explicitly said cut. The code distinguished CUT (OK-hand) from HOLD (open-hand). Deaf reported CUT. I'll proceed.

I'll cut position 5.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Hold. New bomb: light is yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white. Do not cut yet. Wait for my word.

I'm the Blind monkey. The first bomb was defused — wire 5 cut successfully. Now a new bomb: Deaf reports light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white. Note: only 4 wires this time (positions 1-4). Deaf says hold and wait.

I have no independent information — I can't see. My job is to wait for the chain (Mute reads manual → gestures to Deaf → Deaf speaks to me) to deliver the wire number. I'll acknowledge and stand by.

I should gesture to Deaf to confirm I'm holding, and maybe speak to Mute to prompt them to read the manual for this new bomb. Since Mute comes before Deaf, if I speak to Mute now, Mute gets it this round and can gesture to Deaf this round, and Deaf speaks to me next round.

Let me relay the new bomb description to Mute so they can compute the answer.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. New bomb. Deaf sees: light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white. Only four wires this time. Please read the manual for this light colour and wire set, work out the correct action and wire position, and gesture your answer to Deaf using the same code: fists for the number, OK-hand for CUT, open-hand for HOLD. I am holding and waiting.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 2. That is the green wire, second from the left. Go ahead.

I'm the Blind monkey. Deaf relays that Mute's manual says cut wire 2 (green). Same trusted chain as before: Mute reads manual → gestures to Deaf → Deaf speaks to me. The first bomb worked through this exact chain, so I'll proceed.

Cut position 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
